title: plugin-approvals: the approval request page's highlights strip shows the current step's machine id (current_step, such as approve_step) where the approvals get serves the step's label only as step_label
body:
Blocked-by: #24309 (the spec half: `ApprovalRequestRow` declares `current_step_label` — recorded by the triage seat)

**Filing gate ①**, class (a): a user-visible machine name with a named producer on a public door. This is the family's collector card, under the same-family rule. #24264 was the first sighting: the strip's flow chip read `flow:NAME`, fixed by PR #24279. This card covers every other position of the family on the same strip. Filed by `domain:services` seat 1 (seat post #6021) · `marchtian` · `session_01Nk17Z26X5DB59iQztDBADH`, from the #24264 dev's report (`6247309258`, `out_of_scope_findings`). ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and `area:*` are triage's.

- **`reach:`** the served `sys_approval_request_detail` page's highlights strip, on every pending request. The console reads a request through `GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/ID`. This is a static reading of the producer chain, not measured on screen.
- **Reader who acts:** the `domain:services` seat (`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals`), for one dev round.

## The chain, read on `origin/main` `93b4acb57`

- `ApprovalService.openNodeRequest` writes `current_step: input.nodeId` and `current_step_label: labelOrMachineName(input.nodeLabel, input.nodeId)` (`approval-service.ts:3567`–`:3568`).
- The approvals get's row builder serves `current_step` unchanged (`:1171`). It serves the label as `step_label` (`:1183`), not under the declared column name `current_step_label`.
- `sys-approval-request.page.ts` lists `current_step` on the strip. So the "Current Step" chip reads the node's machine id, such as `approve_step`. `sys-approval-request.object.ts:313` describes that column as "Machine name of the step awaiting approval".
- The request lists already show the label: every list view declares `current_step_label` (`sys-approval-request.object.ts:91`, `:100`, `:114`).
- A strip that simply listed `current_step_label` would draw no chip on the routed read, because the get does not serve a field under that name. The approvals face 5 fit-check reading on objectstack-ai/objectui#12491 (`6246163097`) says the same.

## The family's positions on this strip (after PR #24279)

| chip | field | reading |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Flow | `process_label` | fixed by PR #24279 (#24264) |
| Current Step | `current_step` | **the machine id**, as measured above |
| Object | `object_name` | a text field holding the target object's API name. Not measured on screen. If the strip draws it as raw text, it is the same family. |
| Status, Submitter, Updated | `status`, `submitter_id`, `updated_at` | a labelled select, a user lookup and a timestamp: not machine names |

## Wanted

- Every chip on the strip names its subject by a label. The current step chip shows the step's label, with the same fallback the lists use (`labelOrMachineName`: the authored label, else the humanized machine name).
- The page pin (`sys-approval-request-page.test.ts`) holds the strip to label fields. The `object_name` reading is measured and either fixed here or stated as not this family.
- The fix serves the label under a field name the page can list, or names the declared field the get already serves. It says which, and which readers of `step_label` it measured (the console's inbox reads it).
- ⛔ No new column: `current_step_label` is declared.

## Dedupe

- A REST scan of 1032 objectstack and objectui issues updated since 2026-10-01 (open and closed), for `current_step_label`, `current_step` beside chip, strip or highlight, and `step_label` beside `rowFromRequest`, found 2 hits.
  - #23889 (closed) served the step and flow labels to the lists.
  - objectstack-ai/objectui#12491 (closed) is approvals face 5.
- Neither covers the strip's step chip.

Dedupe words: approval request highlights current step machine id; current_step chip approve_step; step_label rowFromRequest current_step_label served; sys_approval_request page strip label.
